title: A Particle Swarm Optimization of an Iterative Function Map for Sustainable Development in Zambia

source.pdf_page_offset_note: PDF page 1 is the summary sheet, PDF page 2 is the title page, and PDF pages 3-20 are internally numbered pages 2-19.

context_sources.use: Page 1 is an official COMAP press release summarizing the sustainability model, 20-year LDC plan, plan evaluation, pertinent data, ecosystem health, social equitability, geographical relevance, and 20-page report context. Pages 2-5 are award tables. The document does not provide the complete official problem statement.

limitations: All 20 paper pages were rendered and visually reviewed; full-resolution checks covered the index equations, maps, tradeoff plot, cellular automata, function graph, optimizer discussion, investment bars, trajectories, sensitivity section, references, and Appendix A.
The extracted text contains encoding artifacts for Greek letters, minus signs, and some symbols, so central equations were read from the rendered pages.
The only authoritative task context located is a results-document press release, not a complete official Problem D statement; official requirement coverage is therefore incomplete.
The appendix table is legible visually but several coefficients and exponents remain insufficiently defined because units and fitted input scales are absent in the paper.
No code, fitted datasets, residual plots, exact optimization outputs, random seeds, or complete PSO configuration are supplied.

official_supported_requirements: Develop a mathematical model for sustainability.
Use the model to produce a 20-year sustainable-development plan for one country on the UN Least Developed Countries list.
Evaluate the effect of the plan on the country's sustainability.
Use pertinent data and consider economic development, ecosystem health, and social equitability.
Provide creative and geographically relevant solutions.
Communicate the work in a 20-page report with data analysis, modeling, methodology, writing, and visualization.
unknown_official_clauses: The complete wording, subquestions, quantitative deliverables, data restrictions, and evaluation criteria are not present in the reviewed context.
Paper-implied objectives beyond the press-release summary cannot be labeled official.
task_reconstruction.paper_approach: Define ecological and socioeconomic indices, infer a cross-country tradeoff, choose Zambia, build a synthetic wealth-population cellular automaton and an iterated cost-to-outcome function network, compare four optimizers, use PSO for a two-stage $1.2 billion example allocation, and recommend a change in the ecological preference weight after ten years.
task_reconstruction.paper_implied_coverage: The paper addresses sustainability measurement, a 20-year Zambia plan, geographic targeting, investment allocation, and qualitative evaluation.
task_reconstruction.coverage_gap: The official statement is incomplete; the ecology index is narrow; transferred dynamics and policy effects are not causally identified; the spatial model is synthetic; core recurrences fail unit and domain audits; optimizer convergence and global optimality are unverified; the plan is only two ten-year decisions; uncertainty, implementation feasibility, and global sensitivity are inadequate.

section_map.summary: Introduces D and E indices, a cross-country tradeoff, a Zambia function map, PSO allocation, and a two-dimensional cellular automaton.
Provides the paper title and team number without substantive content.
Lists the problem, assumptions, two indices, tradeoff, Zambia plan, optimization, sensitivity, conclusion, references, and appendix.
Frames sustainable development and states global-transfer, discrete-funding, deterministic-effect, and air-pollution assumptions.
Adds zero industry growth and perfect spending assumptions and constructs a GWP-weighted air-pollution measure.
Combines normalized pollution and nonrenewable energy equally, maps country values, and acknowledges omitted water and ground pollution.
Defines inequality-adjusted income, life expectancy, education, normalization, logarithm, and subjective component weights.
Maps D values and discusses the benefits and omissions of collapsing economy, health, and education into one index.
Uses a cross-country scatterplot to infer a development path and introduces comparison with an external sustainability index.
Uses seven-of-ten overlap as validation and lists Zambia's initial indices and development features.
Defines wealth diffusion, population growth, mortality, birth, and migration recurrences for a cellular automaton.
Shows synthetic random and corner-biased seeds, claims geographic targeting, and recommends further study of progressive taxation.
Connects program costs to health, wealth, jobs, energy, pollution, D, and E and announces four optimizer families.
Chains global pairwise fits, defines S, criticizes Nelder-Mead and Powell, and describes a genetic algorithm and PSO.
Uses 128 particles, claims likely global optima, reduces annual planning to two decades, and plots investment against sustainability.
Shows example program allocations for three alpha values and fixed-alpha D, E, and S trajectories.
Recommends alpha 0.5 then 1.5, acknowledges two-stage calibration and omitted trade, and begins two local sensitivity perturbations.
Calls expected-direction perturbations robust and claims the model identifies effective 20-year strategies.
Lists peer-reviewed, institutional, and web sources without complete dataset versioning or access metadata.
Lists empirical equations for health, birth, energy, HIV, population, wealth, and jobs, including serious unit and domain ambiguities.

contributions.summary: Decomposes sustainability planning into measurement, tradeoff analysis, country dynamics, optimization, and evaluation.
Attempts to orient an environmental composite so larger values mean better ecological conditions and exposes missing countries on the map.
Attempts to incorporate the distribution of income rather than relying only on mean GDP per capita.
Uses a spatial dynamic illustration to connect wealth and population feedback over time.
Provides a compact dependency view linking policy costs, intermediate variables, and sustainability outputs.
Considers local search, genetic search, and particle swarm search rather than presenting one heuristic without alternatives.
Attempts to communicate both the portfolio and its 20-year outcome path across preference scenarios.
Discloses coarse temporal resolution and omitted trade and performs explicit perturbation experiments.
Collects transition equations in one appendix, making a dimensional and domain audit possible.

nodes.label: Global environmental, development, health, and economic indicators
Nelder-Mead, Powell, GA, and PSO comparison
Fixed-alpha D, E, and S trajectories
Alpha switch, geographic aid, and tax recommendations

missing_edges: No complete official-requirement matrix connects the context to every paper output.
No causal identification connects global cross-sectional fits to Zambia interventions.
No real Zambia spatial layers connect the cellular grid to geographic recommendations.
No stakeholder process determines indicator or objective weights.
No uncertainty model connects data and parameter error to the optimized portfolio.
No coherent dynamic reoptimization connects fixed-alpha scenarios to the recommended alpha switch.
No implementation model connects budget bars to governance, capacity, maintenance, trade, or fiscal feasibility.

assumptions.summary: Only air pollution is material because water and ground data are scarce; this is a convenience assumption that deletes important ecological outcomes.
Zambia follows worldwide development trends; no transportability or local longitudinal validation is supplied.
Funding is discrete, but the final model coarsens the plan to two ten-year allocations.
Spending effects are deterministic, excluding response and implementation uncertainty.
Industry size has zero net change without ICM funding, which amplifies intervention attribution.
All external funding is used fully and correctly, excluding leakage, delay, corruption, and absorption limits.
Income and life expectancy are each weighted twice education based on an unelicited importance judgment and correlation claim.
Alpha represents national environmental preference but has no stakeholder or governance basis.
Appendix equations implicitly assume fit units and support that are not documented.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Per-capita greenhouse-gas emissions are weighted with 100-year GWP values.
Pollution and nonrenewable energy are normalized, equally combined, rescaled, and reversed to make larger E better.
Purchasing power by percentile is multiplied by 1-x and integrated to emphasize lower-income percentiles.
The adjusted-income term is normalized and logged, then combined with normalized life expectancy and education.
Countries missing component data are shown in gray but are excluded from calculations and rankings.
World Bank and other cited sources provide D, E, fertility, health, HIV, inequality, and sector context without a full variable-level provenance table.
WHO, World Bank, and literature data are linearized into pairwise logarithmic, linear, power, and logistic relationships.
Sources mix peer-reviewed literature, institutional pages, and unstable web links without complete versions, access dates, or hashes.
Fitted equations are listed without samples, units for all inputs, coefficient uncertainty, residual diagnostics, or support intervals.

models.summary: A weighted sum of per-capita pollutants uses normalized GWP as the weight.
An equally weighted normalized air-pollution and nonrenewable-energy composite defines E.
A weighted log-normalized inequality-adjusted income, life-expectancy, and education composite defines D.
A cross-country D-E association is used as a hypothesized development trajectory.
Wealth diffusion and population growth and migration evolve on a synthetic two-dimensional grid.
A directed cost network links programs, jobs, health, wealth, energy, pollution, D, and E over time.
D and E are scalarized with alpha as S=(D+alpha E)/(1+alpha).
Nelder-Mead, Powell, a genetic algorithm, and particle swarm optimization are discussed for the allocation problem.
A 128-particle swarm searches program allocations for varying budgets and alpha values.
Fixed-alpha trajectories are interpreted as support for alpha 0.5 in decade one and 1.5 in decade two, without a coherent switch simulation.

verification.summary: Seven-of-ten overlap with similar SSF top-ten lists is treated as validation; full-sample construct and predictive tests are absent.
Qualitative local-optimum, boundedness, runtime, and global-optimum claims are made without equal-budget repeated benchmarks.
The 128-particle result lacks multistart dispersion, convergence traces, seed controls, and optimality-gap evidence.
Agriculture and mining job caps are increased by ten percent and index changes are reported.
Solar is removed and the model substitutes hydropower, which is used as expected-direction robustness evidence.
Independent inspection finds undefined domains, count-rate confusion, negative-state risks, and absent conservation checks.
The paper lacks code, fitted datasets, exact parameterization, seeds, full optimizer settings, and exact portfolio tables.

results_trace.summary: A negative country-level D-E association is found and interpreted as a development tradeoff.
Seven countries overlap in each pair of top-ten lists and this is used to affirm the indices.
Synthetic grids form segregated patterns and motivate targeting poor areas and considering progressive tax.
For a $1.2 billion example, alpha 0.5 yields the highest plotted S near and above the example budget.
Health and education dominate the displayed portfolio, with program mix varying by alpha and decade.
D rises then tapers, E initially falls and later recovers, and S rises under each fixed-alpha scenario.
The paper recommends alpha 0.5 for ten years followed by alpha 1.5 for the second decade.
Small index changes under two perturbations are used to declare solid robustness.
The paper claims ICM can identify highly effective strategies for a successful 20-year plan.

writing_logic.summary: The report gives a readable high-level progression from metrics to country plan to evaluation.
Each index is followed by a strengths-and-weaknesses subsection, which improves local critical structure.
A system diagram acts as the narrative bridge from programs to outcomes and optimization.
The paper discloses coarse temporal resolution and omitted trade before sensitivity analysis.
The conclusion reconstructs the full workflow but overstates causal, spatial, optimization, and robustness evidence.
Collecting equations in one place aids auditing, but missing units and fit details prevent reproduction.

language_observations.summary: Task-first language makes the report easy to scan and provides an effective section-order template.
Words such as encompasses all and sound exceed the narrow measurement and should be replaced with scope-qualified language.
Global optimum language is used without certificates, repeated trials, or bounded gaps.
Matching expectations is used rhetorically as evidence even though the expectations are largely encoded in the model.
Successful and highly effective should be downgraded to exploratory or scenario-based unless the full evidence chain passes.

visualization_observations.summary: The summary includes a model architecture graphic that signals the paper's system-level contribution.
The six-pollutant table places the numerical 100-year GWP weights beside Equation (1), preserving the input-to-formula handoff.
A world map communicates country coverage and marks missing values gray, but lacks data year and uncertainty.
The theoretical and adjusted income curves visually explain the lower-income weighting idea.
The D choropleth supports cross-country comparison but shares the same provenance and uncertainty limitations.
The scatterplot reveals a negative cross-sectional pattern, while the adjacent mean bars risk encouraging causal interpretation.
The side-by-side rankings make the paper's seven-of-ten overlap check visible and auditable, while also revealing that it is a rank-overlap check rather than independent prediction.
Initial, ten-year, and twenty-year panels communicate dynamics but are synthetic and have no geographic coordinates or numeric scale.
The blue and orange dependency graph helps organize the model but does not type arrow semantics or uncertainty.
Figure 7 places three fixed-alpha optimized sustainability curves against investment and marks the $1.2 billion example budget used by the later allocation figures.
The portfolio chart distinguishes decades by fill but has repeated legend labels and no exact amounts or total check.
Three panels compare fixed-alpha paths but suppress y-axis values, uncertainty, and the recommended switched-policy path.
The feature-input-equation table retains all thirteen function-map relationships in one visual registry, including the duplicated row number 3 and low-legibility Jobs exponent.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The official release says judges valued interdisciplinary tools and geographically relevant solutions; the paper visibly integrates environmental, economic, health, spatial, dynamic, and optimization components.
A compact architecture, country choice, named optimizer, and direct policy framing likely improved readability, but award status does not validate the equations or conclusions.

weaknesses.summary: The complete official problem statement is unavailable, so full requirement coverage cannot be established.
Air-only ecology, global-to-Zambia transfer, deterministic effects, and coarse funding are asserted for tractability rather than supported.
Perfect use of external funding excludes leakage, delay, corruption, procurement failure, and capacity limits.
GWP measures climate forcing and is mislabeled as broad environmental damage.
Equal weighting is unexplained and water, soil, biodiversity, resilience, and local exposure are absent.
The log of a normalized term can be undefined at zero and component weights lack elicitation.
Cross-sectional association is treated as a longitudinal causal development path.
Top-ten overlap with similar constructs is weak and partly circular.
Reciprocal life expectancy is used as annual mortality without demographic justification.
Synthetic seeds and grids are not calibrated to Zambia geography.
Geographic targeting and progressive-tax effects exceed the modeled evidence.
Arrows mix causal, associational, definitional, and accounting relationships without distinction.
Pairwise global fits are chained into a dynamic causal network without multivariable identification or uncertainty.
Alpha and component weights encode stakeholder values without a participatory or governance basis.
Claims about bounds, local optima, runtime, and global optima lack equal-budget benchmarks.
A 128-particle configuration has no convergence, seed, multistart, benchmark, or optimality-gap evidence.
The 20-year plan is reduced to two ten-year decisions because of compute limits.
Exact amounts, budget sums, constraints, operating costs, and capacity feasibility are not reported.
Axes omit numeric scales and all trajectories lack uncertainty.
The recommended mid-plan switch is not simulated as one coherent state-carrying reoptimization.
Imports and exports are omitted; fiscal capacity, debt, inflation, and displacement are also absent.
Only two local expected-direction perturbations are tested.
Small expected changes are treated as proof of global robustness and policy stability.
The stated birth-rate formula becomes impossible for ordinary positive GDP values unless an undocumented scale is intended.
Counts, fractions, and percentages are mixed, creating enormous negative wealth factors under literal inputs.
Units, domains, caps, conservation, budget balance, nonnegative states, and numerical stability are not demonstrated.
No code, fitted data, exact seeds, full parameters, or exact optimizer outputs are available.
The final effectiveness claim exceeds the weakest links in the measurement, causal, spatial, dynamic, optimization, and validation chain.

independent_extensions.summary: Replace the two-variable ecological index with a decision-linked multidimensional dashboard and Pareto analysis; retain missing dimensions as bounds or scenarios.
Use a hierarchical panel model to separate within-country transitions from between-country differences and validate transfer to Zambia.
Rebuild the function network as a typed structural causal or system-dynamics model with compatible units, lags, covariance, and intervention semantics.
Calibrate a district-level spatial model from real Zambia population, poverty, infrastructure, ecological, and accessibility layers with spatial holdouts.
Use stakeholder elicitation and Pareto frontiers for D, E, and alpha rather than fixed narrative weights.
Implement annual or receding-horizon robust optimization with state carry-forward, remaining-budget carry-forward, and adaptive reoptimization.
Model leakage, delay, capacity, maintenance, trade, fiscal balance, and implementation failure as explicit stochastic scenarios.
Property-test every recurrence for dimensional consistency, finite values, plausible support, nonnegative states, accounting identities, and timestep stability.
Benchmark PSO against exact relaxations, local-search multistarts, and simple allocation baselines under equal compute budgets and repeated seeds.
Run global sensitivity, structural alternatives, scenario reoptimization, and decision-reversal analysis instead of two local perturbations.
Publish exact allocation tables, machine-readable outputs, code, versions, seeds, convergence traces, and reproducible figures.
Evaluate progressive taxation or other policies with explicit causal pathways, counterfactuals, distributional effects, and implementation costs before recommending them.

candidate_rule_impacts.rationale: Prevent incomplete results context from being mistaken for the full official task.
Preserve the paper's useful decomposition while enforcing end-to-end traceability.
Reverse air-only, GWP-as-damage, equal-weight, and comprehensive-index errors.
Turn convenience assumptions into testable scenarios and non-use conditions.
Block cross-sectional international associations from becoming Zambia causal dynamics.
Require versioned, aligned, locally relevant data and fit provenance.
Prevent temporal coarsening and spliced fixed-alpha trajectories from masquerading as adaptive plans.
Propagate structural, implementation, governance, parameter, and preference uncertainty.
Require exact budget accounting and operational feasibility.
Reverse unsupported comprehensive, causal, geographic, global-optimum, robustness, and effectiveness language.
Catch undefined logarithms and normalization boundary failures.
Catch impossible birth rates, count-rate confusion, negative wealth, and missing state invariants.
Require stakeholder weight elicitation and coherent preference changes.
Prevent synthetic spatial figures from supporting real location advice.
Replace circular top-ten overlap and unreproducible checks with independent validation.
Require real target-country spatial calibration and holdout testing.
Block policies absent from the model from being reported as findings.
Type system-map edges and replace chained pairwise fits with a coherent multivariable system.
Require fair optimizer formulation and compute comparisons.
Require stochastic convergence, multistart, seed, benchmark, and reproduction evidence.
Replace two expected-direction perturbations with global, interaction-aware robustness analysis.
Require exact values, labels, totals, uncertainty, and the actual recommended path in decision figures.
Preserve clear organization while enforcing evidence-bounded strengths, limitations, and conclusions.

unresolved_questions: Can a complete authoritative 2015 Problem D statement be located outside the current corpus?
What units or scale factors were intended in the Appendix A birth, HIV, wealth, population, energy, hydropower, and jobs equations?
Were the country fits cross-sectional, panel-based, or assembled from different years, and what samples and residuals were used?
What PSO inertia, acceleration coefficients, bounds, topology, stopping rule, seeds, and repeated-run results produced the reported allocations?
Do the displayed allocation bars sum exactly to $1.2 billion for each alpha and decade?
Was the alpha 0.5 to 1.5 switch ever simulated as a single state-carrying policy rather than inferred from separate fixed-alpha curves?
